item.description:
Drafta 1.3 makes Preview editable and runs on macOS 15 Sequoia and Intel Macs.

  • Preview is editable. It shows the note as rendered Markdown — tables, images, callouts, formulas and Mermaid diagrams included — and the line with the caret shows its markup while you write. ⌘+click follows a link; a click on a checkbox ticks the task.
  • macOS 15 Sequoia and Intel Macs. One universal build runs on macOS 15 and later, on Apple Silicon and Intel.
  • Typewriter and Focus modes. Typewriter keeps the line you are writing in the middle of the window; Focus dims everything but the current paragraph (Settings → Editor → Behavior).
  • Vim mode. On the Russian layout Normal-mode commands work without switching layouts.
  • Caret settings: blinking speed, width and an optional glide animation.
  • Checklists and statuses in the note list: a progress bar with "14 of 20" under the title, and ▶ ⏸ ✓ ✕ icons for the note's status.
  • One panel button beside the note list's title hides the sidebar, then the note list, and brings them back in reverse; View menu items with ⌃⌘S and ⌥⌘L do the same.
  • Tags: "Tags from text" can be turned off, so only tags added with "+ Add tag" count; a click on a tag in the note header shows where it is written.
  • Emoji in the / menu and as : shortcodes.
  • Edits made on two Macs are merged when they sync instead of one rolling back the other.
  • Import moved to File → Import Notes… (⇧⌘I).
  • Fixed: a window minimized to the Dock now comes back on a click on the Dock icon; wide tables are no longer cut off in PDF, HTML and Word export; one-line formulas render; a toolbar button showing its tooltip presses on the first click; a new note no longer shows a second caret; attachments no longer turn into "(conflict copy)" files on sync.
  • Drafta is now proprietary software.

Drafta 1.2.5 lets you edit Markdown files in place.

  • Opening a .md file from Finder works again. Open, Open With and double-click did nothing: the file never reached the library.
  • The file you open stays linked to its note. Every edit is saved back to the original file as plain Markdown, so you can share the edited file right away, with no export. Images keep their original paths, and images you add in Drafta are copied next to the file.
  • Edits made to the file elsewhere come in the next time you open it in Drafta.
  • A linked file that was moved or deleted is not recreated; the note stays in your library.

Drafta 1.2.4 fixes a gesture conflict.

  • Scrolling a wide table sideways no longer hides the sidebar. A two-finger swipe over the editor shows or hides the sidebar and the note list. It used to fire even when the swipe scrolled a wide table, a code block or the preview sideways. Now a swipe that scrolls content is only a scroll.
  • The panel swipe still works over content that does not scroll sideways, or once a table has reached its edge.

Drafta 1.2.3 fixes empty AI answers.

  • ⌘J no longer comes back empty. A model that thinks (DeepSeek, a local Qwen, OpenAI or Gemini at a reasoning level) could spend the whole answer limit on thinking, and the answer arrived empty and marked as cut off. This happened more often with long notes and prompts typed in the prompt line.
  • Cloud models answer ⌘J with no limit. DeepSeek, OpenAI, Gemini and OpenCode Zen think and answer as long as they need. Claude, whose API requires a limit, gets its model's maximum.
  • Local models keep a limit, with room for thinking on top, so a model that keeps thinking stops within minutes instead of holding your Mac's GPU.
  • Ghost text keeps its short limit, with room for thinking, so suggestions stay quick.
  • If an answer is still empty, the ⌘J window now explains that the model spent its budget thinking and suggests Regenerate or a lower reasoning level.

Drafta 1.2.2 cleans up note previews and brings back the light app icon.

  • Note previews are plain text. The line under a note's title in the list no longer shows Markdown: no **, >, [!NOTE], list bullets, task boxes, link addresses or HTML tags. Code blocks, rules, table separators and lines of tags only are skipped.
  • The app icon follows your Mac's appearance. Drafta shows a light icon in Light mode and a dark one in Dark mode, following System Settings → Appearance → Icon & widget style.

Drafta 1.2.1 fixes sign-in.

  • You stay signed in. At launch Drafta sends several requests at once. If your session had expired, each of them tried to renew it, and the losing request could wipe the new session. Now they share a single renewal. A server that is briefly unavailable no longer signs you out either.
  • The sign-in and unlock screens are always opaque. After you locked the library or signed out, these screens could show through the window's glass effect.

Drafta 1.2 adds local AI models, a model picker for every AI provider, OpenCode Zen and an inline calculator.

  • Local models. A new Local provider works with any OpenAI-compatible server: LM Studio, Ollama or llama.cpp. It needs no key, and your text stays on your Mac. Test connection lists the models on the server.
  • Pick the model for every provider. Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Local and OpenCode Zen load their live model lists, and you can also type a model id.
  • Separate Assistant and Ghost text. ⌘J and the AI commands use one provider and model, ghost text another. For example, Claude for rewrites and a small local model for instant suggestions.
  • Reasoning level per role: Off, Minimal, Low, Medium or High. Off is the default, so ghost suggestions appear instantly and ⌘J costs what it did before. Drafta sends each provider its own setting and never shows a model's thinking in your note.
  • OpenCode Zen. Paste a Zen key to use its low-cost catalogue of Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, Kimi and free models.
  • Inline calculator. Type 1250*12*0,87= and the result appears; Tab or Enter inserts it. It handles + − × ÷ ^, brackets, percentages (15% от 2400=, 2400-15%=), sqrt, round, min, max, and decimal commas or points. It stays quiet in code, maths and links. It replaces the old "Math expressions" option, which never worked.
  • Ghost text never does arithmetic. While you type an expression, ghost text stays silent and leaves the result to the calculator.
  • If a local server is down, ghost text stays silent and backs off, and Settings shows whether the server is unreachable or still loading a model.
  • Fixed: Accept in the ⌘J window could insert the answer again and again without closing. This happened when the answer contained a numbered list.
  • Fixed: AI answers no longer mention the internal [insert here] marker.
  • DeepSeek now defaults to deepseek-flash. The old default model was retired.

Drafta 1.1.1 adds nested tags and fixes a crash.

  • Nested tags. Writing #drafta/blog in a note now gives one tag, drafta/blog, shown as drafta › blog. Before, only blog was kept.
  • Tags as a tree in the sidebar. Fold and unfold branches the way you do notebooks. Selecting a parent tag lists its notes and the notes under all of its child tags.
  • Tags never move notes. A tag with a path used to move the note into a notebook with the same name and silently create that notebook if it was missing. It no longer does.
  • Renaming or deleting a parent tag applies to all its child tags too: drafta → work rewrites #drafta/blog to #work/blog. Tags inside code blocks and inline code are never changed. A note open in the editor shows the new text right away.
  • Tag colours carry over from the old tag names to the nested ones.
  • Deleting a tag from the sidebar always asks first.
  • MCP server:
  • search_notes with a tag also finds the notes under its child tags, and a single word such as blog finds drafta/blog;
  • list_tags shows full paths with note counts;
  • tag_note accepts any spelling of a tag and can remove tags.
  • Fixed: Drafta could crash when you pinned or trashed a note by swiping its row. Pinning twice in a row now leaves the note pinned.

Drafta 1.1 is about speed. Typing, search, launch and switching notes are much faster in large libraries.

  • Typing never stalls. Autosave now updates only the note you edited. Before, it rescanned the whole library, which caused hitches while you typed. In a 5,000-note library each save went from about 150 ms to about 7 ms.
  • Full-text search is instant. Search runs in the background against a prepared index, and the list filter waits for you to pause typing. A search now takes milliseconds instead of more than a second.
  • ⌘P Quick Open returns results as you type. Title matches come first, then matches in note text.
  • Faster launch. The library loads in the background with parallel reads, so a large library opens in a fraction of a second.
  • Instant note switching. The editor now stays loaded between notes. Math, code highlighting and diagrams load only when a note uses them, and the preview redraws only the blocks you changed.
  • New: cycle the view with ⌥⌘P — Editor → Split → Preview → Editor. Your cursor, selection and scroll position stay where they were. ⌥⌘1, ⌥⌘2 and ⌥⌘3 jump straight to a mode, all from the View menu. You can rebind the shortcut in Settings → Keybindings.
  • Safer edits under sync. If sync, an MCP client or another app changes a note while you are typing, your text stays in the editor and a bar lets you choose which version to keep. The other version is saved to the note's revisions, so neither is lost. If the note's file is deleted elsewhere while you are editing it, Keep note restores it with your text.
  • The sidebar counts, the note list and the table of contents no longer redraw on every keystroke.
